assessment: The incumbent achieved the intended course set in 32/40 exports (80%) and a 17-minute median, below the stated targets. Its seven-minute median for unchanged assignments suggests a useful baseline, without establishing causation. Six affected exports coincided with assignment changes; the two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Fast execution and slow replacement delivery suggest a separate coordination delay, but handling components were not measured. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the unsampled split-course center.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for a requested week may omit or misselect courses after an assignment change; selection using the relevant assignment intervals could prevent some affected exports.
openings.delta: Make the requested week relevant to course selection rather than relying solely on present assignments.
openings.prediction: With identical attendance and course identities, changing only the current assignment will change incumbent selection if this mechanism operates; interval-aware selection will retain the agreed weekly course set.
openings.probe: In staging, compare unchanged and midweek reassignment fixtures against coordinator-agreed weekly course sets. Inspect selection before CSV generation, verify the documented CSV schema and tenant isolation, and attempt concurrent attendance entry. Estimate implementation effort and hosting cost before adopting a fix.
assumptions: Assignment history is available or recoverable without guessing.
Coordinators can specify inclusion for a course reassigned within a week.
A production change fits six engineer-days and existing hosting; this is unverified.

openings.claim: Were renamed courses actually absent, or did their exported names fail to match coordinators' timetables?
openings.delta: Distinguish data omission from recognition failure before treating both as export-selection defects.
openings.prediction: Recognition failure leaves the intended course rows present while a name mapping resolves the perceived absence; actual omission leaves expected rows missing even after names are reconciled.
openings.probe: Use a short coordinator session with fabricated renamed-course fixtures, the documented CSV, and old/new timetable labels. Compare expected and exported course identities internally, observe checking and importing, and time these steps separately.
assumptions: Internal course identity can be traced without changing the import schema.
Fabricated tasks provide useful diagnostic evidence but cannot establish production success rates.
